Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D3 levels were statistically significantly associated with depression (BDI-II) among rural adolescents; direction not reported.
Sentence: "There was a statistically significant association between depression and Vitamin D3 levels."
Measured as: depression (Beck's Depression Inventory-II)
Population: 451 rural adolescents aged 11-18 years in government high schools in Kolar, India, excluding those with pre-existing mental illness
Intervention: Measured serum vitamin D3 level (25-OH total), no intervention
Comparator: Adolescents with sufficient vitamin D levels versus insufficient and deficient levels
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 451
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Winter light therapy reduced depression scores in adolescents.
Sentence: "Winter light therapy increases vitamin D (Δ = 8.2 ng/mL, p < 0.001) and reduces depression (ΔPHQ-9=-3.1, p = 0.005)."
Measured as: depression (PHQ-9)
Population: Chinese adolescents in winter RCTs (N = 200)
Intervention: Winter light therapy
Comparator: Not reported
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 7,321
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Study B's exposure is light therapy, not vitamin D supplementation, though it raises vitamin D; Study A is a cross-sectional association, so the pair differs in design, exposure and outcome scale.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"design_or_bias","also_differs":["intervention","population","outcome_measure"],"detail":"design: cross-sectional serum vitamin D association (BDI-II) vs RCT of winter light therapy raising vitamin D (PHQ-9)"}
